spokenText:
Good morning! Here is your daily brief for today.

First, Azure updates. Microsoft has introduced a new version of Azure Firewall that simplifies routing, adds support for more protocols and provides flexible application controls. The goal is to reduce operational overhead while tightening perimeter security for virtual networks.  

In the networking space, Azure Virtual Network Manager IP address management is now generally available in the United States Government and China regions. This gives customers a centralized way to manage IP addresses across multi‑region, sovereign‑cloud deployments.  

The Azure SDK for August 2026 has been released, bringing new libraries and a host of bug fixes that speed up application development and integration with Azure services.  

For developers building secure retail solutions, Microsoft published part two of the 3IQ Retail Assistant demo. The template shows how to place every service behind private endpoints inside a single virtual network, establishing a solid security baseline for new workloads.  

A recent blog post highlights how enterprise AI transformation relies on the end‑to‑end Azure platform. It outlines how Azure networking, storage and security work together to support production‑grade large models.  

On the security front, Microsoft released guidance on securing edge AI in customer‑owned environments. The paper walks through attestation steps to protect AI assets before they interact with sensitive data, an important consideration for hybrid deployments.

Moving on to AI news today, there are no major headlines to report.

Turning to the markets, there are no notable updates in this briefing.

Bottom line: Azure is strengthening its firewall and networking capabilities, expanding IP management to sovereign clouds, refreshing its developer SDK, providing secure demo templates, and reinforcing its role as the backbone for enterprise AI while offering new guidance on edge AI security.

That is your update. Have a great day!
